- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior close.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements; apply a 1–2% upward bias to final 5–7 forecast days if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days and apply downward bias only after sentiment confirms.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before final 5 days.
